_comment: Past releases, newest first. The current one comes from app/src/main/assets/release/release.json; make_docs.py merges both into the in-app Release Notes (assets/help/release_notes.json) and docs/Release-Notes.md.

versions.summary: Folder Refresh, protected system folders and the feature tour
new: Refresh under Phone storage and SD card lists folders made since, marked New.
"Take a tour of the features" opens once after you install or update OmniFind.
improved: System folders (Android, LOST.DIR, hidden folders) and other apps' files are never listed or read.
fixed: A folder reached through a link, or a path back into Android/, is refused.
The caution before indexing says PDFs, not pdfs.

versions.summary: Android 15 to 17, every screen density and large text
new: Launcher icon in every density, with round and themed (Android 13+) versions.
improved: Edge to edge on Android 15 to 17: nothing under the status or navigation bar.
Layouts hold from small ldpi screens to tablets, in landscape and at 200% text.
"All files access" on Android 11 and later; notification permission on 13 and later.
fixed: The privacy note no longer covers the examples on short screens.
Buttons, tags and chips no longer cut words off at large text sizes.
Thumbnails are sharp on every density.

new: Search documents (txt, md, html, docx, odt), PDFs, photos and screenshots by what's in them, in your own words and across languages, with exact words, numbers and names matched as written.
Choose the kinds of file and the folders to search, on the phone and on the SD card.
Files already indexed are skipped; nothing is read or embedded twice.
Indexing in the background while the phone charges, with progress and a Stop button.
PDFs open at the page that matched; pictures open in your gallery.
The model downloads inside the app, once, over Wi-Fi, checked before it's used.
Runs entirely on the phone's processor, from Android 9 on, tested on a 2017 Xiaomi Mi A1.
versions.thanks: Thank you, Abdur Rahim. OmniFind exists because of DigUp, Abdur Rahim's open-source app that searches the files on your computer by what's in them with EmbeddingGemma 2. DigUp showed what this model can do for everyday files, and its open code made OmniFind possible: the way OmniFind runs the model, ranks meaning against exact words, and reads documents and pictures follows DigUp's, and its reference vectors are how we checked that a phone finds the same things a computer does.
